newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares bounce back, seen strong.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares bounce back, seen strong.

text.p: Slovenian shares resumed their upward path on Wednesday, overcoming a brief sputter at the start of the week, and traders forecast further gains were in store for the SBI index.
The seven-share SBI rose 10.82 points or 0.86 percent to 1,265.4 points, helped by demand from foreign investors. Turnover rose to 610.7 million tolars from 464.3 million.
"Shares will probably continue rising to the end of the year. The extent will depend on how much foreign money is in the market," said Karmen Cerar of brokerage Poteza.
Overall 13 shares rose, eight fell and one was unchanged. Two shares were untraded.
SKB was the most actively traded share, following reports that the bank may raise foreign investors' equity stake to 49 percent from 30 percent.
SKB shares closed down 90 tolars at 41,500 on volume of 6,430 lots and turnover of 272.6 million tolars. Earlier they hit a high of 43,100 on an early wave of buying.
Trading company Kovinotehna was the biggest gainer, firming 10 percent to 484 tolars on volume of 1,420 shares for total turnover of 664,800 tolars.
Bank UBK was the leading decliner, falling 8.75 percent to 7,300 tolars on volume of 43 shares for total turnover of 313.900 tolars.
Drug maker Lek's "A" issue was steady at 20,500 tolars on volume of 8,843 shares for total turnover of 184.1 million tolars. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
